scope: For the Section 5 continued-fraction decoder, the integer recurrence maintains coprimality, a positive denominator and bounded numerator/denominator. Computing index t takes at most t+1 quotient levels.

At every index, including after an exact rational terminates, the Euclidean recurrence agrees with Mathlib’s Real.convergent. It already produces the reduced denominator, as needed for the order test after Eq. (5.13).
Invariant for the Section 5 implementation that keeps the least positive passing denominator. It updates the minimum when another candidate is inserted, using zero for the empty set.

Exact algorithmic refinement of Section 5 continued-fraction postprocessing. Scanning t integer convergents and testing denominators by binary modular exponentiation yields the reference minimum over verified real convergent denominators, or zero if there are none.

The actual scan counts its Euclidean frames and modular multiplications. For clock width L and budget 2L+1, their bounds are (2L+1)(2L+2) and 2L(2L+1), respectively. This supplies an explicit arithmetic-work bound for Section 5 postprocessing.

At each visited Euclidean frame the operands and intermediate numerator products and sums are at most the clock size Q, and both unreduced products in each modular multiplication frame are below N². These width bounds complement the polynomial arithmetic counts.
